        <script>
        function dayCount(targetISO){
          const now = new Date();
          const target = new Date(targetISO);
          const ms = target - now;
          if (ms < 0) return "DONE";
          const d = Math.ceil(ms / (1000*60*60*24));
          return d + (d===1 ? " day" : " days");
        }
        document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", () => {
          document.querySelectorAll("[data-final]").forEach(el => {
            el.textContent = dayCount(el.getAttribute("data-final"));
          });
        });
        </script>

## Strategy at a glance

::: {.panel-tabset}

### IR 362 — heaviest weight, essay format

**Strategy:** Build *six* essay-bank thesis statements you can deploy across any of Hammad's 17 study-guide questions. The questions are not independent — they revolve around the **API → Abraham Accords pivot**, the **Nash equilibrium "carousel,"** and **Iran's linkage role** between the two regional spheres. Master those three throughlines and the 17 questions become recombinations of the same material.

Reading order:

1. [Final Run](ir362/final-run.qmd) — low-clutter path: recall, check, repair, write
2. [Framework with all 17 questions](ir362/index.qmd) — the full reference spine
3. [Iran & the Axis](ir362/iran-axis.qmd), [Abraham Accords](ir362/abraham-accords.qmd), [Nash Equilibrium](ir362/nash-equilibrium.qmd), [Syria Collapse](ir362/syria-collapse.qmd) — the four deep-dive research pages
4. [Hammad's 7 Frames](ir362/frames/index.qmd) — Bellin, Brownlee/Masoud/Reynolds, Mitchell, Gause, Diwan/Malik/Atiyas, Sayigh, Bayat
5. [Primary Sources](ir362/sources/index.qmd) — Balfour → Abraham Accords text
6. [Mock Essays + Sample Answers](ir362/mock-essays.qmd) — demonstrations for structure and calibration
7. [Cram Sheet](ir362/cram-sheet.qmd) — final-night condensation

::: {.callout-warning}
**Source-coverage gaps to flag with Hammad's syllabus:**

- **Q10 Nash equilibrium**: Hammad assigned a specific article + slide. **Check Brightspace.**
- **Q16 Iran/Hezbollah/Syria**: deep-dive triangulates Nasr / Parsi / Goodarzi / Norton — confirm against syllabus.
- **Q6 + Q13/Q14 (Syrian collapse + carousel)**: lecture-based; carousel is Hammad's own framing.
:::

### ECON 205 — Mon May 11, 2:00–4:00 PM

**Strategy:** Cumulative final, ~70% post-midterm material. Pencil + calculator only. The exam tests *application* — given a scenario, can you pick the right model and execute the algebra. Cram-sheet memorization happens *before* exam day, not on it.

5-day plan (Wed May 6 → Mon May 11):

| Day | Focus | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|
| Wed 5/6 | Read Cram Sheet · run Active Recall §1 (pre-midterm) | 30 cards correct in a row |
| Thu 5/7 | Active Recall §2 (Money/Inflation, Fluctuations, Fiscal) | Mock Exam A diagnostic |
| Fri 5/8 | Mock Exam A under timed conditions · review key | Identify 5 weak spots |
| Sat 5/9 | Killer Traps · drill the 5 weak spots | Trap-drill score ≥ 80% |
| Sun 5/10 | Mock Exam B under timed conditions · review key | Net error rate ≤ 10% |
| Mon 5/11 | Light skim of Cram Sheet · 90 min walk · sleep · exam | — |

Start here: [ECON 205 overview](econ205/index.qmd)

### ACCT 410x/410 — Mon May 11, 4:30–6:30 PM

**Strategy:** Leventhal "user-oriented" — emphasize *what the number means for a manager*, not journal-entry mechanics. The USC Registrar lists Accounting 410 in the Monday May 11, 4:30–6:30 PM exception slot; verify Hanna's section against Brightspace. The April 20 tutoring brief identified four high-yield trap areas (indirect cash flow, multi-product CVP, inventory error reversal, bond pricing). Drill those first.

Start here: [ACCT 410x/410 overview](acct410x/index.qmd)

### Marketing — Ensemble project, syllabus pending

**Strategy:** Treat this as a deliverable, not a memorization exam. Until the syllabus arrives, the honest work is to build the pitch spine: target user, problem, competitive set, positioning, evidence, go-to-market, and risk answers.

Start here: [Marketing overview](marketing/index.qmd)
